Your buildings

Building selects an independent project with its own floors, rooms, connections and view. Manage lets you create, duplicate or rename a building, add or rename floors, File opens older layouts from Archive. L0 is the permanent ground-floor code; its name is editable. Undo and redo stay with the building while this tab is open.

Edits save locally in this browser on this device. File exports one building or a complete building backup. Import always creates new copies; it never replaces your current building. Keep a downloaded backup before clearing browser data or changing devices.

Stairs and floors

Stairs + creates an aligned stair stack across the floors you check. Select an existing room, then Convert to stairs in the inspector or its right-click menu to keep its footprint. Preview shows the required size, real elevations, flights, landings, skipped floor openings and any warnings before saving. Select an existing stair and choose Edit connected floors to extend its stack. Move and resize linked stairs together. New stairs still need doors into adjacent rooms at the floor arrival end. The stair inspector checks these doors against the landing.

The left floor list works like pages: click a floor, add one with +, or use Edit floor to rename it or change its elevation. Building management and the legacy archive are above the list. The sun/moon button toggles light and dark. On a phone, Inspector lets you hide or show the detail panel for more drawing space.

Direct drawing tools

Selection is the default: click a room or connection. Drag a room to move it, or any orange edge or corner to resize. Drag a door or passage along its shared wall. Right-click a room to change its type, or a connection to change its type or delete it. The current type is checked. With a room or connection selected, Shift+F10 opens the same menu; use the arrow keys and Enter. Hold Space or use middle-mouse drag for temporary pan. Release Space to return to selection. On touch screens, drag empty paper to pan and use two fingers on empty paper to zoom.

Hold C to connect: drag from one room into another, or tap two rooms. A green shared-wall preview shows a valid connection. Choose single door, double door or open passage in the always-visible Connections panel. Single doors start at 1.2 m and double doors at 2 m. Changing back to single resets its width to 1.2 m. The clear-width slider changes in 0.1 m steps and stays within the shared wall. A drag is one Undo step; Escape cancels it. Double doors have two leaves and a total clear width. Open passages have no door leaf.

Hold X to disconnect: click a connection, or drag between two connected rooms. Hold P to draw a room: drag a rectangle, snapped to 0.5 m with a 1 × 1 m minimum. Release C/X/P to return to selection. Releasing a key during a drag cancels the unfinished edit. Escape cancels and returns to selection. The tool buttons work for one action on touch screens.

Delete / Backspace removes the selected room or connection. Rooms without connections delete immediately. Other room deletions confirm how many connections will also be removed. Undo restores the entire change. Typing in fields never triggers drawing shortcuts.

Linked stairs move and resize together on every level in their stack; local transfer stairs stay local. Legacy misalignment is preserved until you explicitly edit that stack. Courtyard and Operations voids follow their source room and cannot be moved separately. Freight shafts retain their existing locks. Actual overlapping room areas are shown in red; intentional void/shaft cutouts are excluded. The lower-floor stack overlays each lower above-ground level at 10% opacity. Current floors are solid and mask the stack; real voids remain open. Basements show only lower basement levels. Toggle the stack and dimensions in View. File contains JSON/SVG export and import; level notes and the legend are in the inspector. Switching floors preserves your view. Stair flights, treads and landings are calculated from actual elevations; UP and DOWN routes are drawn separately. The stair inspector shows clear widths, risers and headroom checks. Required slab, services and ceiling cutouts remain design requirements; this is not a construction or runtime-traversal certification. Corridors are editable rooms too. Plan checks flag overlaps, detached doors and rooms without a route to a floor entrance.

Undo / redo: Ctrl or ⌘ Z / Shift Z. Arrow keys move a selected room 0.5 m. SVG export produces editable vector linework for Figma; JSON preserves the complete editable model.
